newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-PLAY SUSPENDED IN U.S. OPEN DUE TO LIGHTNING.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PLAY SUSPENDED IN U.S. OPEN DUE TO LIGHTNING.

text.p: The second round of the U.S. Open was temporarily suspended on Friday by the threat of lightning in the vicinity of Congressional Country Club.
Play was halted at 11:52 a.m. EDT (1552 GMT) when lightning was detected in the area, just west of Washington.
About 60 players in the 156-man field had yet to tee off when the siren sounded to stop play.
Colin Montgomerie of Britain, the first-round leader at five under par, was among those who had not started play when the suspension was called.
Tom Lehman, the British Open champion, was one stroke off the lead at four under after playing 16 holes of his second round.
